title: Spatial storage trends
note: 2003–2023 common available months within each basin; calendar-month fixed-effect OLS. These differ from full-record seasonal Sen slopes. GLDAS land storage excludes groundwater and surface water. Each panel has its own scale; the three storage definitions are not interchangeable.

title: National temporal comparison
note: Separate panels retain different storage definitions. Top: observed and naturalized total storage. Bottom: matching land compartments. Gaps are retained; no direct full-TWS error is assigned to partial GLDAS land storage.

title: TWSA climate reconstruction for all 22 basins
note: Naturalized parent-model target and frozen meteorological ensemble reconstruction. Green shading identifies the held-out 2016–2023 period; earlier values are training or validation context. The emulator targets a hydrological model, not independently observed storage.

title: Matched GLDAS time series for all 22 basins
note: Matched soil + canopy + snow anomalies in mm. GLDAS and WaterGAP share climatic influences. Agreement evaluates land-component consistency; it cannot validate groundwater or the entire human residual.

title: Spatial RMSE by evaluation target
note: Pooled 2016–2023 metrics. Climate reconstruction targets naturalized TWSA; the climate baseline is separately compared with observed GRACE TWSA; land storage is compared with matching GLDAS compartments. Pair counts differ because GRACE has gaps. Compare basins within the same panel, rather than ranking models across different targets.

title: Annual RMSE through time
note: Years 2016–2023; at least eight paired months are required per annual score. GRACE mission-gap years may have no score. Shading describes variation among basins, not a confidence interval. Each panel has its own vertical scale and evaluation target.

title: Annual RMSE for all 22 basins
note: All three explicitly labelled evaluation targets are retained. Different targets and compartment variances prevent interpreting a smaller cross-target RMSE as a better climate model. Missing annual scores remain gaps.
